        Assistant: There are two sizes that are relevant when talking about CPU's. The size of the silicon and the package. The size of the package is determined mostly by the pincount. About the die size: It's not exactly static, either. Of course the dies never where bigger than the packages. However there where times when the chips got so big that they couldn't fit in the classic package. That's when the L2 cache was put in extra packages and the whole thing was put together as a cpu module. AMD did that with the Athlon and intel with the Pentium2 and early Pentium 3. Moore's law then ensures that the dies will shrink back down again. If anything the question should be: "why do CPU's stay the same size and not become smaller?"
